text: Which wells were down longest this summer, and why? For an engineer, that simple question reaches across inspections, repairs, manuals, and people's notes.
Measurements tell us what was observed. Maintenance records explain what happened. Standard operating procedures explain what should have happened. Corrections can change what we know.
The design principle is simple: language helps ask the question; evidence supports the conclusion. The model selects tools, while versioned records and deterministic calculations supply the facts.

The interface combines Next dot J S with Open U I, giving engineers private conversations, inline visuals, and an evidence drawer. Fast A P I coordinates Gemma and three governed tools. PostgreSQL stores the authoritative facts, rules, and saved results. Neo four J and Mem zero provide recall projections. The nao analytics sidecar is optional and outside the default path.

Every source keeps its file hash, path, and version. Record versions retain their original line references, so reimporting never erases history. Rules come from cited manuals and procedures. Asset query returns typed rows with evidence identifiers. Recall results searches only the current user's saved work. Propose feedback prepares a correction, but explicit human confirmation is required before publishing it.
Here is the first recorded example. Michael Turner asks which rules well zero zero zero one has broken in the last twelve months, and which issues remain open.

The result separates each protocol from the evidence. Written notice took forty one hours, against a twenty four hour limit. Containment took about seven hours, against four. The table also identifies the agency verification deadline and the outstanding regulatory response. Each finding can be traced to its source.

Look at spill response rule S R zero one. A reportable spill requires written notice within twenty four hours of discovery. The regulator record shows forty one hours. A separate record contains the open five thousand dollar notice of violation. The rule and the recorded event are both needed to support this conclusion.

Some evidence exists only in prose. The repair report says the release was contained about seven hours after the inspection flight. That supports comparison with the four hour procedure limit. The copilot preserves the report citation alongside the finding, so the engineer can inspect the original wording rather than trust an unsupported summary.

Open actions are shown separately from completed work. Where a response is not recorded, the answer says that it is not recorded. It does not invent a response or assume an action happened. Pending root cause analysis and missing shutdown records remain visible. The annual flowline test is recorded as complete. This walkthrough illustrates saved sample results rather than a live browser interaction.
Now Michael reports that the September twenty fourth spill at well zero one five one was measured at five point four barrels, rather than the original four point five estimate.
That statement creates a draft, not an immediate overwrite. Validate the well, inspection, value, and units. Show the before and after values, record the reason, and require explicit confirmation.

After confirmation, Laura queries the shared record. Five point four barrels crosses the five barrel reporting threshold. The result flags the notice deadline and the absence of a recorded written notice.
The audit trail keeps both values, the author, and the reason. The correction stays effective months later. Earlier saved answers remain reproducible, while fresh queries use the accepted value.

Private memory has a different boundary. Jessica asks about the three wells discussed yesterday. She has no matching private discussion, so the copilot says so. It never borrows Michael's conversation or silently turns an unresolved reference into a fleet wide query.

Michael asks the same question. His own saved result identifies the original three wells. The copilot can recover that exact set and calculate current repair costs with citations. Shared corrections affect the facts, while ownership checks keep each engineer's private discussion separate.
Eighteen scenarios passed deterministic replay. Live model evaluation remains. PostgreSQL stays authoritative. This is an illustrated walkthrough with synthetic narration.
